findings.issue_text: pkg/storage/unified/search/bleve.go:72 — BuildIndex no longer holds cacheMu for the whole build, so two concurrent calls for the same key can both build an index (wasted work, resource/file-handle leak) and race to overwrite b.cache[key], silently dropping one built index (and its open file-backed bleve index) with no Close() call

pkg/storage/unified/resource/server.go:308 — initWatcher() now runs after search.init(), so if search.init() blocks a long time indexing large resource sets, initWatcher's subscription to backend.WatchWriteEvents starts later, widening the gap during which any events emitted between server construction start and broadcaster setup are not captured by the server's own Watch() stream (mostRecentRV also updates later)

pkg/storage/unified/resource/server.go:258 — NewResourceServer now runs s.Init(ctx) synchronously (search index build + watcher start) at construction time with no timeout, so a slow/unavailable backend (e.g. GetResourceStats hanging) blocks server/process startup indefinitely instead of the server becoming available and lazily initializing per-request

pkg/server/module_server_test.go:35 — New t.Skip for postgres ("test not working with postgres in Drone. Works locally") added alongside making Init synchronous/mandatory in NewResourceServer, masking rather than fixing an apparent regression where eager Init at construction fails/hangs under postgres in CI

pkg/storage/unified/search/bleve.go:137 — BuildIndex no longer holds cacheMu for the duration of the (expensive) index build, only around the final cache map write; combined with getOrCreateIndex's lack of per-key locking (search.go:287 TODO), concurrent callers for the same uninitialized key can now race to build the same file-backed bleve index directory concurrently, risking on-disk index corruption/lock contention that the previous coarse lock serialized away

pkg/storage/unified/search/bleve.go:72 — BuildIndex mutex scope was narrowed (no longer covers index construction/build, only the final cache write) with no test added to verify concurrent BuildIndex calls on the same key behave correctly

pkg/storage/unified/resource/server.go:258 — Init(ctx) moved from being called lazily/idempotently on every RPC to a single call in NewResourceServer's constructor, with no test asserting RPCs behave equivalently if called immediately after construction or that init errors still surface correctly

pkg/storage/unified/resource/server.go:293 — initWatcher() reordered to run after search.init() instead of before, changing startup ordering with no test covering the new sequencing or that watch events aren't missed/duplicated during index build

pkg/server/module_server_test.go:36 — The one existing integration test that exercises module server startup/init (TestIntegrationWillRunInstrumentationServerWhenTargetHasNoHttpServer) is skipped for postgres in the same PR that reorders Init logic, removing the test most likely to catch an Init-ordering regression

pkg/storage/unified/search/bleve.go:137 — No test exists anywhere in the repo for bleveBackend.BuildIndex verifying cache correctness under concurrent calls for the same key (e.g., duplicate index builds, lost writes, or races on b.cache)

goldens.comment: A race condition in BuildIndex allows multiple goroutines to concurrently build the same expensive index for the same key. This is caused by moving the b.cacheMu lock from protecting the entire function to only protecting the final cache assignment.

Calling s.search.TotalDocs() here may race with concurrent index creation: TotalDocs iterates b.cache without synchronization, and the event watcher goroutine started just above could trigger BuildIndex writes concurrently, potentially causing a concurrent map read/write panic.

adjudication_records.issue_text: pkg/storage/unified/resource/server.go:308 — initWatcher() now runs after search.init(), so if search.init() blocks a long time indexing large resource sets, initWatcher's subscription to backend.WatchWriteEvents starts later, widening the gap during which any events emitted between server construction start and broadcaster setup are not captured by the server's own Watch() stream (mostRecentRV also updates later)

adjudication.rationale: The diff verifiably changes Init() ordering in pkg/storage/unified/resource/server.go so that s.search.init(ctx) runs before s.initWatcher() (lines around 300), whereas previously the watcher started first. Since search.init() can plausibly take a long time (building/indexing), this can delay watcher/broadcaster setup. However, the specific claim about missing events for the server’s Watch() stream and mostRecentRV updates depends on initWatcher()/WatchWriteEvents semantics that are not shown in the diff, so the data-loss impact isn’t strictly provable from the provided changes alone.

adjudication_records.issue_text: pkg/storage/unified/resource/server.go:258 — NewResourceServer now runs s.Init(ctx) synchronously (search index build + watcher start) at construction time with no timeout, so a slow/unavailable backend (e.g. GetResourceStats hanging) blocks server/process startup indefinitely instead of the server becoming available and lazily initializing per-request

adjudication.rationale: The diff shows `NewResourceServer` now calls `s.Init(ctx)` synchronously during construction (pkg/storage/unified/resource/server.go), and per-request lazy `s.Init(ctx)` calls were removed from most RPC handlers. `Init` runs one-time setup including `s.search.init(ctx)` (which may build an index) and then `s.initWatcher()`. This can indeed delay (or potentially hang) server construction/startup if dependencies are slow, but the diff alone does not prove an actual defect (it may be an intentional fail-fast/ready-at-startup change), nor does it show what `ctx` is (deadline/timeout unknown).

adjudication_records.issue_text: pkg/server/module_server_test.go:35 — New t.Skip for postgres ("test not working with postgres in Drone. Works locally") added alongside making Init synchronous/mandatory in NewResourceServer, masking rather than fixing an apparent regression where eager Init at construction fails/hangs under postgres in CI

adjudication.rationale: The diff clearly adds a new `t.Skip` for `dbType == "postgres"` with the comment that it fails in Drone but works locally, which does mask a CI-only failure instead of addressing it. The diff also makes initialization eager/mandatory by calling `s.Init(ctx)` inside `NewResourceServer` and removes per-RPC `Init` calls, so tying the skip to a potentially impactful init timing change is a reasonable review concern. However, the claim that eager `Init` specifically “fails/hangs under postgres in CI” is not directly verifiable from the diff alone.

adjudication_records.issue_text: pkg/storage/unified/search/bleve.go:137 — BuildIndex no longer holds cacheMu for the duration of the (expensive) index build, only around the final cache map write; combined with getOrCreateIndex's lack of per-key locking (search.go:287 TODO), concurrent callers for the same uninitialized key can now race to build the same file-backed bleve index directory concurrently, risking on-disk index corruption/lock contention that the previous coarse lock serialized away

adjudication.rationale: The diff in pkg/storage/unified/search/bleve.go removes holding cacheMu across the entire BuildIndex operation (the lock/unlock at the top is deleted) and now only locks around the final b.cache[key] assignment. From the diff alone, that does make it possible for concurrent callers to proceed through an expensive index build in parallel for the same key if cache lookup happens before BuildIndex without additional synchronization, which could be problematic especially for the file-backed bleve.New(dir, ...) path. However, the diff does not show the cache lookup / get-or-create logic (nor the cited TODO in search.go) needed to verify that duplicate builds for the same key can actually occur, so the risk is grounded but not fully provable as a definite defect from this snippet.

adjudication_records.issue_text: pkg/storage/unified/search/bleve.go:72 — BuildIndex mutex scope was narrowed (no longer covers index construction/build, only the final cache write) with no test added to verify concurrent BuildIndex calls on the same key behave correctly

adjudication.rationale: The diff in pkg/storage/unified/search/bleve.go removes the cacheMu Lock/Unlock that previously wrapped the entire BuildIndex function and now only locks around the final `b.cache[key] = idx` write. This is a real, diff-grounded concurrency/behavior change: concurrent BuildIndex calls for the same key could now both build indexes in parallel and race to populate/overwrite the cache. The finding’s point about the narrowed mutex scope is verifiably true from the diff; whether this is an actual correctness bug can’t be confirmed from the diff alone (it may be an intentional throughput improvement), but it is a substantive review concern and the diff adds no concurrency-focused test coverage.

adjudication_records.issue_text: pkg/storage/unified/resource/server.go:258 — Init(ctx) moved from being called lazily/idempotently on every RPC to a single call in NewResourceServer's constructor, with no test asserting RPCs behave equivalently if called immediately after construction or that init errors still surface correctly

adjudication.rationale: The diff does move initialization from per-RPC lazy calls to eager construction: `NewResourceServer` now calls `s.Init(ctx)` and returns an error if it fails (pkg/storage/unified/resource/server.go around +255), while the explicit `s.Init(ctx)` calls were removed from RPC handlers like Create/Update/Delete/Read/List/Watch/Search/etc. The finding’s concern is about missing regression/behavioral tests covering this nontrivial semantic shift (init now happens at construction time and init failures surface earlier), which is a concrete review issue but not a verifiable functional defect from the diff alone.

adjudication_records.issue_text: pkg/storage/unified/resource/server.go:293 — initWatcher() reordered to run after search.init() instead of before, changing startup ordering with no test covering the new sequencing or that watch events aren't missed/duplicated during index build

adjudication.rationale: The diff in pkg/storage/unified/resource/server.go reorders initialization in Init(): search.init(ctx) now runs before initWatcher() (the watcher-start block was moved below the search init block). That is a real sequencing change visible in the diff, and it could affect whether write events occurring during index initialization are observed/handled in the same way as before. However, the diff alone doesn’t prove missed/duplicated events (it depends on how search.init and the watcher interact), so it’s not a verifiable defect—more a legitimate concern about behavioral change lacking explicit coverage.

adjudication_records.issue_text: pkg/server/module_server_test.go:36 — The one existing integration test that exercises module server startup/init (TestIntegrationWillRunInstrumentationServerWhenTargetHasNoHttpServer) is skipped for postgres in the same PR that reorders Init logic, removing the test most likely to catch an Init-ordering regression

adjudication.rationale: The diff explicitly adds a postgres skip to the integration test `TestIntegrationWillRunInstrumentationServerWhenTargetHasNoHttpServer` (`if dbType == "postgres" { t.Skip(...) }`), reducing coverage for postgres. In the same PR, initialization behavior/order is changed in `pkg/storage/unified/resource/server.go` (e.g., `NewResourceServer` now calls `s.Init(ctx)` and RPC methods no longer call `Init`), so skipping one of the few startup/init integration tests for a DB backend is a concrete, diff-grounded testing/coverage concern rather than a directly verifiable functional defect.

adjudication_records.issue_text: pkg/storage/unified/search/bleve.go:137 — No test exists anywhere in the repo for bleveBackend.BuildIndex verifying cache correctness under concurrent calls for the same key (e.g., duplicate index builds, lost writes, or races on b.cache)

adjudication.rationale: The diff changes bleveBackend.BuildIndex locking behavior (removes cacheMu lock around the whole function and only locks around b.cache[key] = idx), but the finding claims "No test exists anywhere in the repo" for concurrent cache correctness. Repository-wide test absence cannot be verified from this PR diff alone, so the claim is not diff-grounded.
